title: benchmark evidence (v1)
description: Outcome vocabulary for the benchmark lane. Benchmark artifacts publish p50/p95/p99 distributions under cold and warm conditions with full host metadata. Benchmark results are NEVER a binary pass/fail gate: a 'pass' field on a benchmark would encode a hidden SLA and obscure the actual distribution. This schema forbids any 'pass' field at every level via additionalProperties:false and an explicit not-required rule. Use blocked_reason on the benchmark item to record unavailability; downstream reviewers compare the recorded distribution against the declared target_ms, not against a boolean.

not.description: Fail-closed rule: a benchmark artifact MUST NOT carry a top-level 'pass' field. additionalProperties:false already rejects unknown top-level keys; this not-required clause is kept explicit so the prohibition is greppable and survives a future refactor that loosens additionalProperties.

class.description: Constant discriminator. Every benchmark evidence artifact sets this to 'benchmark' so downstream tooling can branch on lane without parsing the file name.

host_metadata.description: Snapshot of the host substrate at benchmark time. Required so every p50/p95/p99 is reproducible and reviewable: the same distribution on different hardware means different things. Capture as much as the host exposes; never lie about nested or cgroup-v2.

cpu.description: CPU model string as reported by /proc/cpuinfo 'model name' (or platform equivalent). Include enough detail to identify stepping and microarchitecture when possible.

kvm_api_version.description: KVM_GET_API_VERSION at benchmark time. Stored as -1 when /dev/kvm was inaccessible so the field is always present.

page_cache_state.description: Page-cache state at the start of each measurement. 'cold' means caches were dropped between samples (drop_caches=3), 'warm' means caches were primed with the workload, 'mixed' means the bench described its own policy in artifacts. Per-sample state belongs in benchmark items.

memory_size_mib.description: Total host RAM in MiB. Used to contextualize VM memory and to verify the bench respected host limits.

vcpu_count.description: Logical CPU count available to the orchestrator (nproc). Used for parallel sample scheduling and for the scheduler determinism tests.

cgroup_v2.description: True iff the host runs a unified cgroup-v2 hierarchy and the orchestrator parent exposes cpu+memory+pids. False disables any benchmark that depends on resource limits.

nested.description: True iff nested virtualization is available. Required for the direct-KVM subset; documented for Firecracker comparisons.

benchmarks.description: Per-benchmark distribution records. Each item is a single named measurement (e.g. 'snapshot_create', 'snapshot_restore', 'warm_http_first_call') with its declared target_ms, the unit of the percentiles, the cold/warm distribution, and a blocked_reason if the benchmark could not run. NEVER encode a boolean pass; reviewers compare the recorded distribution against target_ms.

not.description: Fail-closed rule: a benchmark item MUST NOT carry a 'pass' field. Mirrors the top-level rule so the prohibition is greppable at every nesting level where a contributor might be tempted to add one.

target_ms.description: Reference target in the unit declared below. Treated as metadata, not a pass/fail threshold. The plan forbids claiming a universal '<200 ms' guarantee; targets are documented per workload and host.

unit.description: Unit of the recorded percentiles and of target_ms. Typically 'ms' for latency or 'rps' for throughput. Reserved units are listed for tooling convenience.

p50.description: 50th percentile of the recorded samples in 'unit'. Nullable when the benchmark was blocked (see blocked_reason).

p95.description: 95th percentile of the recorded samples in 'unit'. Nullable when the benchmark was blocked.

p99.description: 99th percentile of the recorded samples in 'unit'. Nullable when the benchmark was blocked.

cold.description: Cold-condition distribution. 'cold' means caches were dropped before each sample (or per the harness policy recorded in artifacts). Required even when the benchmark is blocked; in that case samples=0 and the percentiles are null.

samples.description: Number of cold-condition samples collected. The plan requires N>=100 when the bench is unblocked; samples=0 indicates a blocked or skipped cold phase.

warm.description: Warm-condition distribution. 'warm' means caches and any pre-loaded artifact are reused across samples; record samples>=100 when unblocked.

blocked_reason.description: Stable token explaining why this benchmark could not produce real samples (e.g. 'kvm_unavailable', 'docker_missing', 'page_cache_drop_unsupported'), or null when the bench ran. Pair this with cold.samples=0 and warm.samples=0 when blocked; do not fabricate samples.
